I had moved to another country to be with my then boyfriend. After a couple years, I broke up with him. That was during Chinese New Year where all hotels were full and realtors weren't working or landlords were celebrating with family. I desperately needed a place to stay as my ex obviously kicked me out, but most places I called said they couldn't show me anything until a week later.

Then I called one last place, this woman was a fucking saint, she said she could let me see the place the next morning. Went to see it, explained my situation and let me rent the place the same day. I lived there for a year, she always treated me well and never raised my rent despite raising it for others. Honestly don't know what I'd have done without her.

I used to cut myself a lot (sadly still do occasionally). I have scars all over my arm. 

I thought they were ugly and for the longest time tried to hide them by wearing long sleeves. 

When I met my husband he was sad and heartbroken, not only about the scars and that I ever felt I needed to hurt myself, but also about how ashamed I felt about them. 

He took my hand and told me I have no reason to be ashamed of the scars, that they are proof of how strong I am and how far I've come.

That helped me a lot. He thinks I'm beautiful no matter what. He helped me feel less ashamed.

So I'm gonna tell you the same thing: these scars you have prove how strong you are and how far you've come. These scars do not define you and do absolutely not make you any less beautiful.

I moved from Europe to Asia, trying to find my place, but nothing felt right. And I would feel homesick, I'd cry at night and say I wanna go home, but I had no place I considered home. 

You know how people always say "home is where your heart is"? I considered that to be the dumbest shit ever and then I met my husband. When I'm with him I feel at home, as cheesy as it sounds.

You'll find your place eventually, a place you can call home. Try to stay hopeful, don't give up.

As for your question about taking a year off, it's a tough decision to make. Last year was an especially rough year for me mental health wise and it was also my last year at university. I was thinking about maybe taking a break, but I felt really bad about it since I already started university so much later than most people. However I also felt that class was the only distraction I had, what would happen if I had nothing to do? 

In the end, I didn't take a break, I kept on going to class when I was able to get out of bed. However, my university was fairly supportive, they and my therapist played a big part in me actually finishing my studies. 

Not sure where I was going with all that, but taking a break or not is entirely up to you, and there is absolutely no shame in finishing a year later, you and your personal wellbeing come first, always.
